articles.title: Singapore's top university destroys tumors with magnetic pulses, no chemo needed
articles.content: Researchers at the National University of Singapore have used brief pulses of a weak magnetic field to eliminate breast tumors in 75% of the mice they tested, without any chemotherapy.

articles.title: Chinese nationals face 40 years over kidnapping of Singaporean at Malaysia airport
articles.content: They face one count under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961, read with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which covers acts carried out with common intention. Conviction carries 30 to 40 years in prison and caning.

articles.title: Humans must become wiser to coexist with AI 'species'
articles.content: Last June, I taught a class on AI at a summer camp for 60 students aged 12 to 20.

articles.title: Tech workers spiral into anxiety, exhaustion because of 'age 35 curse'
articles.content: Shutting his laptop at 3:00 a.m. with vision blurred after a grueling 16-hour shift, 27-year-old The Vinh found sleep impossible, his limbs trembling with fatigue.

articles.title: US colleges are so short of students they're admitting people who never applied
articles.content: Hundreds of U.S. colleges are admitting high school students who never applied, as the number of American 18-year-olds begins a long decline.

articles.title: Passengers wait for 6 hours to collect baggage at Thailand's largest airport amid heavy flooding
articles.content: Passengers arriving at Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport had to wait up to six hours for their bags, while luggage from several flights was left behind amid disruptions to Thai Airways's ground operations.

articles.title: Rush-hour downpour freezes HCMC traffic
articles.content: Heavy rain during Wednesday afternoon's rush hour caused severe traffic congestion around Tan Son Nhat Airport, while floodwaters quickly rose across many parts of Ho Chi Minh City.

articles.title: Lost shark becomes viral star in South Korea, boosts sales and named ambassador
articles.content: A wayward shark has unexpectedly become a celebrity in South Korea, attracting large crowds, praise from a local mayor and even affecting the stock market.

articles.title: Passengers taking international flights from Long Thanh airport to pay $25 service fee
articles.content: Passengers departing on international flights from Long Thanh Airport will pay a US$25 service fee from October 1, matching the fee at Hanoi's Noi Bai Airport and exceeding Tan Son Nhat's fee by $5.

articles.title: World's largest bullet-train network grows by 1,142 km ahead of National Day rush
articles.content: China opened four high-speed railway lines totaling 1,142 kilometers on September 28, expanding the world's largest bullet-train network before the National Day holiday rush.

articles.title: Heavy rain, flooding snarl Ho Chi Minh City traffic during morning rush hour
articles.content: Heavy rain and flooding caused major traffic congestion on multiple routes into downtown Ho Chi Minh City during Wednesday morning's rush hour.

articles.title: Australian woman dies after cosmetic surgery at HCMC international hospital
articles.content: A 65-year-old Australian woman died after undergoing cosmetic surgery at City International Hospital in Ho Chi Minh City's An Lac Ward, according to the municipal Department of Health.

articles.title: World's second richest country to give one million households utility rebates in October
articles.content: Singapore will provide more than one million eligible households living in public flats with utility rebates worth S$110-190 in October to help ease living costs.

articles.title: Casino billionaire sells home for $8.9M in world's most expensive residential market
articles.content: Casino billionaire Angela Leong On-kei sold her luxury detached house in Hong Kong for HKD70 million, or about US$8.9 million.

articles.title: Dollar slips against dong
articles.content: The U.S. dollar weakened slightly against the Vietnamese dong on Wednesday while remaining on track to finish September higher against major currencies.

articles.title: Gold prices gain
articles.content: Vietnamese gold prices increased on Wednesday morning even as global gold prices headed toward a 6% monthly decline.

articles.title: World's richest woman grows $33B richer in a year without running a company
articles.content: Alice Walton, the world's richest woman, gained US$33 billion in wealth within a year despite not running a company of her own.

articles.title: Bus, train fares in Asia's richest country to rise 7%
articles.content: Adult commuters in Singapore will pay more for bus and train rides from December 26, with fares rising 7% amid higher energy costs.

articles.title: Luckin Coffee has 100 outlets in Southeast Asia's smallest country
articles.content: China's largest coffee chain, Luckin Coffee, has opened its 100th store in Singapore after only three years in the market.

articles.title: Singapore's 6-year-old homegrown patisserie to shutter by year-end
articles.content: Singaporean patisserie LUNA plans to close at the end of December 2026 after six years, citing rising operating and ingredient costs and changing consumer spending habits.

articles.title: How exposure to dead peers may accelerate aging in fruit flies
articles.content: Researchers have found that exposure to dead members of the same species can trigger biological changes in fruit flies that are associated with faster aging.

articles.title: Chiefs of US chip giants Nvidia, AMD join advisory board of Asia's top university
articles.content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD CEO Lisa Su have joined an advisory board at Tsinghua University's School of Economics and Management in China.

articles.title: World's second-richest country brings semiconductor education to primary schools
articles.content: Singapore is introducing semiconductor education in primary schools through a two-year pilot program designed to help students understand coding, AI and the role of chips in modern technology.

articles.title: World's top university builds swimming robot powered by living muscle cells
articles.content: Engineers at MIT have developed a paper-thin swimming robot powered by living muscle cells rather than a conventional motor.

articles.title: Exploring Vietnam's first climate heritage site, a century-old church
articles.content: The ruins of Hai Ly church on Xuong Dien beach in Ninh Binh have become a popular attraction after being recognized as Vietnam's first climate change heritage site.
